name: SPH liquid tank
doc: A few thousand SPH particles (double density relaxation on the GPU, uniform-grid neighbours) slosh in a glass tank, drawn as one smooth liquid surface from splatted density with a bump-lit rim, glints, foam where it moves fast and glowing spray. Bass drives a paddle at the left wall that pushes waves across; kicks tilt and jolt the tank (the liquid feels the turn and the shove as inertia); every onset throws up a crown splash; loudness brightens it.

palette.doc: stop 0 is the backdrop, the middle stops the liquid from deep to shallow, the top stops rims, foam and glass

count.doc: number of particles (rounded to 256); the particle spacing shrinks to keep the same volume

substeps.doc: sim steps per tick: fewer is cheaper but bouncier

gravity.doc: gravity in tank units per second squared (the tank is 1.6 x 0.9)

stiff.doc: pressure stiffness: higher is less squashy (and less stable at few substeps)

near.doc: near pressure: keeps particles apart, gives surface tension-like drops

visc.doc: viscosity: 0 is water, high is syrup

fill.doc: liquid volume as a share of the tank (before it settles a little)

waves.doc: how far the bass drives the wave paddle in

sway.doc: slow idle rocking, radians: keeps quiet tracks moving

size.doc: tank size on screen (1 = the tank's height fills 90% of the screen)

blob.doc: splat radius in particle spacings: bigger is smoother and rounder

thresh.doc: surface threshold on the normalised density

foam.doc: white foam where the liquid moves fast

cycle.doc: palette drift of the liquid, sweeps per 16 beats
